triplets.head: Arthur Cecil Pigou

triplets.head: The Economics of Welfare
triplets.tail: Divergence between marginal private and marginal social net product causes market failure; corrective tax internalizes externality

triplets.tail: The Problem of Social Cost (1960, Journal of Law and Economics, Vol. 3, pp. 1–44)

triplets.head: The Problem of Social Cost
triplets.tail: If property rights are clearly defined and transaction costs are zero, parties bargain to efficient outcome regardless of initial rights assignment

triplets.head: Martin L. Weitzman
triplets.tail: Prices vs. Quantities (October 1974, Review of Economic Studies, Vol. 41, Issue 4, pp. 477–491)

triplets.head: Prices vs. Quantities
triplets.tail: Under uncertainty, relative slopes of marginal abatement cost (MAC) and marginal damage (MD) curves determine whether price or quantity instrument is welfare-superior

triplets.head: Prices vs. Quantities
triplets.relation: application to climate — stock pollutant argument
triplets.tail: CO₂ is a stock pollutant with effectively flat marginal damage in any single year plus steep abatement costs → tax preferred

triplets.head: Prices vs. Quantities
triplets.relation: application to climate — tipping point caveat
triplets.tail: Near climate tipping points marginal damage curve becomes nearly vertical → cap preferred
